summary:
Radar for 2026-11-13, GLP-1 focus. The biggest fresh event is the FDA's NAION warning order of 9–10 Nov, which adds NAION to the Warnings and Precautions section of every GLP-1 label, including Mounjaro and Zepbound. FDA's figures are about 6.4 vs 3.8 per 100,000 per year. Mainstream news has covered it heavily, but explainers written for tirzepatide users with a calm label angle are still thin. It fits the "label change explained" format.

The second fresh hook is the T-REx randomized trial (Nature Medicine, 10 Nov). It enrolled 120 adults aged 50–70 without diabetes for 40 weeks. Resistance training cut lean-tissue loss by about 25% for the same weight loss, and strength rose about 10% vs fell about 10% without training. This is a randomized result that can anchor a broad "Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) muscle loss" long video. It shouldn't be a single-trial deep dive.

Third, Foundayo's ATTAIN-OSA results (JAMA plus AHA, 9 Nov) and its China approval (12 Nov) push up "foundayo" search demand. Use the label only for what-to-expect, and say the sleep apnea use isn't approved.

Stopping or rebound coverage is surging (Fox News, ACSH, Medscape, plus New York Post "psychiatric symptoms after stopping" headlines). The NY Post psychiatric claims rest on case reports, so fold them carefully into a broad "keeping results after stopping" video and don't make them their own topic. Thanksgiving peaks 18–27 Nov.

Evergreen search formats stay the long-form backbone: first month on tirzepatide, pen and injection-site how-to, nausea, hair loss, and a Foundayo vs tirzepatide approved-drug comparison.

Watch ObesityWeek (14–17 Nov). If the full REDEFINE 4 (CagriSema vs tirzepatide, randomized) or another randomized head-to-head goes public, that triggers a 48-hour fast-turn video. The topline has been known since Feb, so expect modest demand.

Rejected: dose-stretching or skipping-doses stories, compounded price reports, gray-market retatrutide, and employer coverage cuts.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound) new eye warning: the FDA NAION label change explained
candidates.angle: A calm label-change explainer. It covers what NAION is (sudden, usually painless vision loss, often in one eye), FDA's numbers (about 6.4 vs 3.8 per 100,000 people per year, rare), the fact that FDA found no mechanism, and the AAO's guidance. Viewers should report sudden vision changes right away. Don't stop the medicine on your own; talk to your prescriber. Avoid fear framing and lawsuit angles.
candidates.predicted_peak: 0–7 days (news peak now; search tail 4–8 weeks as label updates appear)
candidates.why_now: FDA ordered the warning on all GLP-1 labels on 9–10 Nov. It's in BBC, CNBC, USA Today, Fox, The Hill and the AAO, and lawsuit stories are adding a second wave. Coverage is news-led, and few calm 'what it means if you're on tirzepatide' explainers exist. It fits the label-change search format.

evidence.signal: FDA to require NAION risk warning on GLP-1 therapies (9 Nov 2026)
FDA orders GLP-1 label changes over vision loss risk
Warnings and Precautions section; about 6.4 vs 3.8 per 100,000 per year; no mechanism identified
AAO: what you need to know about the FDA's new GLP-1 warning (11 Nov)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) muscle loss: what keeps it. Anchored by the T-REx randomized trial (Nature Medicine, 10 Nov 2026)
candidates.angle: Broad 'how to keep muscle on tirzepatide' video. T-REx enrolled 120 men and postmenopausal women aged 50–70 without type 2 diabetes for 40 weeks: resistance training three times a week vs no training, with both arms getting hydration, protein and fibre advice. Weight loss was about the same (about 22 kg in both arms). The training arm lost about 25% less lean tissue, and strength went up about 10% with training vs down about 10% without. Add protein and practical starter routines. These are averages; check with your prescriber before a new routine.
keywords: how to keep muscle on mounjaro
candidates.why_now: A fresh randomized result, the first RCT of tirzepatide plus resistance training. It's in UWA, RACGP newsGP and News-Medical but hasn't reached mainstream US news or creators. Muscle loss is a top worry for GLP-1 users, and Strength is already a 606-min long-form we can link to.

evidence.signal: T-REx: 120 adults aged 50–70 without T2D, 40 weeks, 25% less lean loss, strength +10% vs −10%
Resistance exercise to attenuate lean mass loss during tirzepatide therapy for obesity: RCT
Trial registration NCT07457437

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) first month: what to expect, week by week (label and trials, no dosing)
candidates.angle: A what-to-expect timeline: appetite and 'food noise' changes, when GI side effects tend to show up (often around dose increases) and ease, realistic early weight change from SURMOUNT averages, hydration, and the emergency signs to watch for. The label's oral-contraceptive note covers the first 4 weeks and each dose increase. Describe the escalation schedule only as 'your prescriber increases it gradually', with no amounts.
candidates.predicted_peak: steady; seasonal lift late Dec–Jan (New Year starts)
candidates.why_now: Owner-listed top priority and one of the search formats that beat channel averages by 10–195x. Prescriptions are still growing (Foundayo and tirzepatide records), and New Year starters arrive in about 6 weeks, so publishing now lets it rank by January.

evidence.signal: Broad timeline video 'How Long' earned 233 min; first-month video is listed as a priority
Tirzepatide demand drove Lilly to raise guidance, showing a large and growing starter population

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound) pen and injection sites: how-to from the Instructions for Use
candidates.angle: A device how-to taken only from the official IFU: site choices (stomach, thigh, upper arm with help), rotating sites, letting the pen reach room temperature if the IFU says so, what the clicks and grey plunger mean, and storage and disposal. Cover single-dose pen vs KwikPen (UK/AU) differences at the device level only. No amounts, no 'extra dose' tricks. Close with the injection-site reaction rates (6–8% vs about 2% on placebo).
candidates.predicted_peak: steady; lift with New Year starters
candidates.why_now: Device how-tos are a proven 10–195x search format in this niche. Injection-site Shorts reached 238 and 160 views (above median). The BBC 'GLP-1 overdose' piece (12 Nov) shows interest in pen use, and we can answer it with a correct-use video.

evidence.signal: 'What happens when you overdose on GLP-1s' (12 Nov): demand for pen-safety content
Injection-site topic in 8 snapshots at momentum 88

candidates.topic: Keeping results after stopping tirzepatide (Mounjaro): SURMOUNT-4, rebound worries and what helps
candidates.angle: A broad, reassuring video built on SURMOUNT-4: 335 vs 335 randomized, +14.0% regain on placebo from week 36 to 88, and placebo still ended 9.9% below starting weight. Then the habits linked to holding on (strength training, protein) and planning any change with your prescriber. Address the 'rebound' and 'psychiatric symptoms after stopping' headlines in one honest chapter: these come from case reports, causation isn't established, and mood changes need a call to your clinician. No stopping or tapering advice.
keywords: what happens when you stop zepbound
candidates.why_now: Fox News '6 rebound risks after stopping' (12 Nov), ACSH 'Taking GLP-1s forever?' (12 Nov), and NY Post plus several outlets on psychiatric symptoms after stopping (11–12 Nov) are stacking on Medscape (7 Nov). Our Stopping video is 235 min by day 8, so this can be a refreshed or broader follow-up or linked as Watch next.

evidence.signal: Ozempic and Zepbound users face 6 rebound risks after stopping (12 Nov)
Discontinuation of GLP-1s tied to psychiatric risk (observational / case-level)

evidence.source: Primary Care Companion for CNS Disorders
evidence.signal: Case report: mood and psychotic symptoms after rapid discontinuation (2 cases)

candidates.topic: Thanksgiving on tirzepatide: feeling full fast, protein first, smaller plates, alcohol and nausea at the big meal
candidates.angle: Funnel Shorts from 18 Nov pointing to the existing Thanksgiving long-form: one practical question each (feeling sick after a big plate, the 'sulfur burp' after pie, alcohol and low blood sugar if you're on insulin or sulfonylureas). Use no dates in narration.
candidates.why_now: In 11 consecutive snapshots at 90–93. The seasonal peak starts in 5 days. An early post (6 Nov) got 20 views, so hold Shorts until 18 Nov.

evidence.signal: Seen 11 times, momentum 90–93

candidates.topic: Foundayo (orforglipron) what to expect, plus ATTAIN-OSA sleep apnea results (JAMA/AHA, 9 Nov)
candidates.angle: Label-only what-to-expect for the approved pill (how it's taken per label, common GI effects, who it's for). Add a short 'what's confirmed' segment on ATTAIN-OSA: 52 weeks, AHI −17.8 vs −4.5 on placebo without PAP. It isn't approved for sleep apnea; Lilly plans to file by end of 2026. Tirzepatide (Zepbound) is approved for moderate-to-severe OSA with obesity, as context.
candidates.why_now: ATTAIN-OSA in JAMA and AHA (9 Nov), China approval (12 Nov, many outlets), a new Foundayo campaign, and 'foundayo' is already our top non-EloraTZP search term (312 min, 121 from search). Few creator explainers yet.

evidence.signal: ATTAIN-OSA: oral GLP-1 linked to fewer breathing interruptions
Foundayo reduced OSA severity up to 44%; FDA filing planned by year-end
Lilly first with GLP-1 weight-loss pill approved in China (12 Nov)

candidates.topic: Foundayo vs tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound): pill vs weekly shot, what the labels and trials show
candidates.angle: Approved-drug comparison against tirzepatide, built from each label and pivotal trial (ATTAIN-1 vs SURMOUNT-1, both without diabetes). Cover how each is taken, average weight loss, common side effects and who might discuss which with a doctor. Be explicit that this is a cross-trial comparison, not a head-to-head, with no switching advice.
keywords: foundayo vs mounjaro which is better
candidates.why_now: Approved-drug comparisons against tirzepatide are a proven high-performing format. The pill's China approval and US prescription records (12 Nov) are raising 'pill vs shot' questions, and the Wegovy pill has passed 8M prescriptions.

evidence.signal: Lilly beats Novo to China with an oral GLP-1 for obesity
AHA26: orforglipron vs oral semaglutide on predicted CV risk

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide nausea: why it happens, when it usually eases, what helps
candidates.angle: A felt-symptom Short or chapter: slower stomach emptying, nausea tends to cluster around dose increases and fade, smaller meals, stopping at first fullness, less greasy food. Name the red flags: severe ongoing belly pain with or without vomiting (possible pancreatitis) means call your healthcare provider right away. Optional context: genetics (GIPR variant, Nature, April 2026; association only) may partly explain why it hits some people harder. Don't call that study new.
keywords: why does mounjaro make me nauseous
candidates.predicted_peak: steady; lift over the Thanksgiving meals
candidates.why_now: A visible felt-symptom search format; the nausea Short got 179 views (above median). Holiday meals make it more urgent.

evidence.signal: Nature GWAS: GIPR variant linked to nausea and vomiting on tirzepatide only

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide hair loss: is it normal? (new angle: who it affects more)
candidates.angle: A Short that runs once the Hair long-form is verified. New angle: the label rates by sex (women 7.1% vs men 0.5%; placebo 1.3% vs 0%; overall 5.4% vs 0.9%), the link with fast weight loss, that shedding is often temporary, and when to see a doctor. Point the related-video link to the Hair Loss long video.
keywords: does hair grow back after mounjaro
candidates.why_now: Our best Short ever (1,024 views) was hair. Allowed once a week, and the related-video link is still unset.

evidence.signal: Hair grow-back Short 1,024 views; Hair long at 63% average view

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide injection site reactions: redness, itching, small lumps. Is it normal?
candidates.angle: Calm 'Is this normal?' Short: label rates of 6% (5 mg) and 8% (10 and 15 mg) vs about 2% on placebo. Rotating sites helps. Serious allergic reactions are post-marketing reports, and trouble breathing or swelling of the face or throat means emergency help. Related-video link to Side Effects.
candidates.why_now: Seen in 8 snapshots at 88. The two injection-site Shorts reached 238 and 160 views.

evidence.signal: Seen 8 times, momentum about 88

candidates.topic: Fast-turn watch: ObesityWeek (14–17 Nov) randomized head-to-heads vs tirzepatide (full REDEFINE 4: CagriSema vs tirzepatide 15 mg)
candidates.angle: Only if full randomized data go public during ObesityWeek: a 'Did CagriSema beat tirzepatide?' extra L2 within 48 h. REDEFINE 4 was open-label, 84 weeks, 809 adults with obesity: 23.0% vs 25.5%, and non-inferiority wasn't met. Lead with what's new in the full data (side effects, body composition), since the topline dates from Feb 2026.
candidates.why_now: ObesityWeek starts tomorrow. The fast-turn 'Did X beat tirzepatide?' model earned 44% of all watch time (EloraTZP), but only when the result was genuinely fresh. Topline-known reruns flopped (CagriSema 117 min), so ship only if the full data are new.

evidence.signal: Zepbound bests CagriSema in REDEFINE 4
CagriSema fails non-inferiority vs tirzepatide (topline Feb 2026)

candidates.topic: Retatrutide and knee osteoarthritis pain: what's confirmed (TRIUMPH-4 and TRIUMPH-1-OA, NEJM)
candidates.angle: 13:00 lead Short on new Phase 3 data: about two-thirds on retatrutide reached at least 50% knee-pain reduction vs 38% on placebo, with up to about 25% average weight loss at the top dose. Retatrutide isn't approved, and the gray-market versions are unsafe; never point to sources.
candidates.why_now: Still circulating (News-Medical, Newsmax, Health and Me, 10–12 Nov). Retatrutide Phase 3 Shorts get 82–280 views, but momentum is declining across 5 snapshots.

evidence.signal: A weight-loss drug eased knee arthritis pain in two major trials (10 Nov)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide burping and heartburn: why sulfur burps and reflux happen and what helps
candidates.angle: Felt-symptom Short, or a chapter inside a broad 'foods that make Mounjaro side effects worse' long video: slower stomach emptying, big or fatty meals, lying down soon after eating, carbonated drinks. Say when to call (persistent heartburn, trouble swallowing).
candidates.why_now: Seen in 11 snapshots at 74–80. Holiday meals make it more relevant. A narrow symptom, so it works better as a Short or chapter than as its own long video.

evidence.signal: Seen 11 times combined, momentum 74–80

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide dehydration on sick days: the label's kidney warning heading into flu season
candidates.angle: A Short pointing to the Dehydration long video: vomiting or diarrhoea can dehydrate you, and the label warns of acute kidney injury. Cover signs (dark urine, dizziness, very little urine) and why to call your prescriber if you can't keep fluids down. No medication-change advice.
candidates.predicted_peak: rises Dec–Jan with stomach bugs and flu
candidates.why_now: Seasonal illness is starting, and the Dehydration long video needs funnel support before its day-7 check on 11-17.

evidence.signal: Seen twice at 82

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and alcohol: what the label says, plus fresh incretin and alcohol-use-disorder research
candidates.angle: Funnel Short to the Alcohol long video (shipped 11-12): less craving is often reported, and early trials in alcohol use disorder are promising but this isn't an approved use. Include the low-blood-sugar caveat for people on insulin or sulfonylureas. Never give a 'safe amount'.
candidates.why_now: MedPage (12 Nov): a novel GLP-1 cut heavy drinking days in alcohol use disorder. A Ther Adv Psychopharmacol review supports this, and holiday parties are coming.

evidence.signal: Novel GLP-1 cut heavy drinking days in alcohol use disorder (12 Nov)
Systematic review: incretin therapies for alcohol use disorder

candidates.topic: REJECT: 'GLP-1 users skip doses and stretch supply', compounded tirzepatide price reports, gray-market retatrutide, employer coverage cuts (Deloitte)
candidates.angle: Don't cover. Dose-stretching invites self-titration. Compounded and gray-market sources are banned, and cost or coverage topics are banned and underperform.
candidates.why_now: Heavy coverage on 10–12 Nov (Bloomberg, Ozari/Join Luma releases, AJMC gray-market retatrutide, Business Insider on Deloitte), but all of it falls outside the brand's guardrails.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 users skip doses, stretch supply amid cost pressures
